name: Rota basis conjecture
question: Can n bases of an n-dimensional vector space be arranged into a grid where each row and column is a basis?
first_attack: Audit precise statement and prove a restricted case
method_title: Replay the object, or mine the census
dispatch_next: Quotient instances by the stabiliser of the standard basis so that GF(2)^4 becomes exhaustive, storing one grid certificate per orbit.
dispatch_why: Chan (1995) covers rank at most 3. The next experiment is the orbit quotient that makes the rank-4 case GF(2)^4 exhaustive.

campaign.method: Exhaustive grid search over GF(p)^n with GL-symmetry reduction
campaign.hypothesis: Any n bases of an n-dimensional vector space can be arranged in an n x n grid whose rows are the given bases and whose columns are bases.
campaign.first_proof_obligation: Specify the next finite case not yet covered here (GF(2)^4) with an orbit-reduced instance count and a per-orbit certificate format.
campaign.next_experiment: Quotient instances by the stabiliser of the standard basis so that GF(2)^4 becomes exhaustive, storing one grid certificate per orbit.
campaign.falsification: n bases of GF(p)^n with an exhaustive certificate that no valid grid exists.
campaign.blocker: GF(2)^4 has about 10^8 raw instances; orbit reduction under the stabiliser is not implemented yet.

probes.name: Rota basis conjecture
probes.title: Rota's basis conjecture: exhaustive grids over GF(p)^n
probes.frontier: Known: true for every matroid of rank <= 3 (Chan 1995) and other special cases; open in general. These cases are reproductions only.

smoke.scope: Every choice of n bases of GF(2)^2, GF(3)^2, GF(5)^2, GF(7)^2, GF(2)^3 admits a Rota grid (B_1 fixed by GL-transitivity).

deep.scope: Every choice of n bases of GF(2)^2, GF(3)^2, GF(5)^2, GF(7)^2, GF(2)^3, GF(3)^3 admits a Rota grid (B_1 fixed by GL-transitivity).

milestones.title: Rota's basis conjecture verified exhaustively for GF(2)^2, GF(3)^2, GF(5)^2, GF(7)^2 and GF(2)^3
milestones.description: Every choice of bases (first fixed by GL-transitivity) has a certified grid; basis counts match |GL(n,p)|/n!. The deep run adds all 1,753,128 instances over GF(3)^3.
